23 A sound wave is detected by a microphone. The output from the microphone is connected to the
Y-input of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (c.r.o.). The trace on the c.r.o. is shown.
The time-base is set at 0.20 ms per division.
What is the frequency of the sound wave?
A
1000 Hz
B
1250 Hz
C
2000 Hz
D
2500 Hz

hints: Count the horizontal divisions for one complete sine wave on the c.r.o. screen, from the same point on the wave to the next identical point.
Multiply that number of divisions by the time-base of $0.20 \text{ ms}$ per division to get the period $T$ in $\text{ms}$.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ converted to seconds to find the frequency in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify one full cycle on the trace, for example from one upward crossing of the centre line to the next upward crossing.
Count its horizontal length. It spans 4 divisions on the c.r.o. grid.

A.explanation: Gives $T = 1.0 \text{ ms}$, which is 5 divisions and does not match one full sine wave on the trace.

B.explanation: One period is 4 divisions, so $T = 0.80 \text{ ms}$ and $f = 1/T = 1250 \text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Gives $T = 0.50 \text{ ms}$, which is only 2.5 divisions and is shorter than one complete cycle shown.

D.explanation: Gives $T = 0.40 \text{ ms}$, which is 2 divisions and corresponds to about half a cycle, not a full period.
